CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in both hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling lasting several weeks. Symptoms began after a car wreck in December when patient broke both wrists. Patient notes the tingling and numbness became more noticeable after the fractures healed. He describes the symptoms as primarily soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly with hand use. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring finger up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring finger. Tingling is more prominent when symptomatic but becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but reports possible decreased sensitivity. Patient also reports mild neck stiffness dating to the accident when he sustained a head contusion. Symptoms have worsened over the past month. Patient wears splints on both wrists, particularly the right which is worse. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medicine but has not been taking it regularly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. GI: excessive appetite and bloating. Endocrine: reports always being hungry. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems is negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Car accident with bilateral wrist fractures in December. Head contusion from motor vehicle accident. Prediabetes, now controlled with diet modifications. No thyroid issues.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medication (prescribed but not taking as directed).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. Motor vehicle accident in December.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination performed. Right hand: sensation normal except pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers. Left hand: sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ at knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, possibly bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome, though symptom presentation more consistent with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome attributed to past wrist trauma causing nerve irritation. Plan: Schedule EMG test to determine exact location of nerve irritation and pinpoint the issues. Patient to return for follow-up visit after testing. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options. Continue wearing splints.
